claims.text: The TaVCrW alloy is equiatomic, corresponding to approximately 25 at.% each of Ta, V, Cr, and W.
The solid state of TaVCrW is BCC.
The standard TOR-TILD baseline uses an EAM reference potential and thermodynamic integration.
Replacing EAM and TI with an MTP and FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
The MTP+FEP method can maintain sub-meV free-energy accuracy.
Accurate reproduction of the DFT phase-space distribution by the MTP enables TI to be replaced by FEP.
An MTP trained on DFT data can reproduce the local atomic environments of solid and liquid TaVCrW with sufficient fidelity for free-energy sampling.
The MTP can model the electronic density of states near the Fermi level.
Electronic-excitation effects associated with a DOS gap or shift at the Fermi level materially affect the free energy and melting point of TaVCrW.
Short-range order stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
The SRO stabilization energy arises from local chemical ordering in the liquid/solid interfacial region.
FEP can directly calculate the solid-liquid free-energy difference while avoiding the slow convergence of TI.
Magnetic fluctuations, particularly those associated with Cr, contribute to the TaVCrW free-energy landscape at high temperature.
Longitudinal spin-fluctuation methods can represent finite-temperature magnetic states and magnetic contributions to free energy in multicomponent alloys.
A temperature range of 2000-2400 K is sufficient to observe the TaVCrW phase transition.
A supercell containing more than 200 atoms is required to capture the correlation length and stabilization energy of SRO.
The TaVCrW melting point is expected to lie between 2100 and 2300 K.
Sub-meV free-energy accuracy corresponds to less than 10 K uncertainty in the predicted melting temperature.
The usual GGA-PBE underbinding and LDA overbinding rules fail for V and Cr at 0 K and may propagate errors into high-temperature free energies.
NbMoTaW is an established equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy that can be used as a benchmark system.
